name: Magarac (Donkey)
description: Magarac (literally 'Donkey') is a high-speed, lighthearted card-passing game popular in Croatia, Serbia, and the wider Balkan region. Similar to the Western game 'Spoons' or 'Pig', it is a game of reaction and physical speed. Players pass cards around the table attempting to collect four of a kind, after which a frantic 'slam' follows to avoid being the last person noticed.
deck: Standard cards adapted to player count

history.origins: A regional Balkan evolution of the 19th-century matching games. It shares roots with the English 'Pig' and the German 'Schweinerei'.
timeline: 1900s: Fast card-passing games become common in village gatherings.
1950s: The 'Magarac' variant with its specific donkey-themed forfeits is standardized.
Present: A primary social game for children and teenagers in Southeast Europe.
2000s: Digital arcade versions appear on regional gaming portals.
history.cultural: In Croatia, getting the full 'M-A-G-A-R-A-C' letters often results in a funny forfeit, like imitating a donkey's bray.
history.evolution: The game was simplified to use only specific ranks (e.g., only 4 Aces/Kings/Queens for 3 players) to maximize the speed of each round.

setup.deck: Use 4 cards of the same rank for each player. (e.g., 4 players = 16 cards total).
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 4 cards face-down.
setup.equipment: Standard deck, tokens for spelling MAGARAC.

rules.objective: Avoid being the last player to react when a set is completed.
rules.gameplay: 1. Players simultaneously pass one unwanted card from their hand to the player on their left. 2. This continues rapidly until one player collects all four cards of the same rank.
keyRules: Pass cards simultaneously to the left
Collect four of a kind to trigger the slam
Last to react loses the round

strategy.basic: Keep your eyes on the group, not just your cards. Most players in Magarac lose because they are too focused on trying to complete their own set and don't notice the person next to them has already slammed.
strategy.intermediate: The Stealth Pass: If you need only one card and you see the person to your right is about to pass it, prepare your slam hand. As soon as the card touches your fingers, slam itâ€”don't even look at it! If you were right, you win; if not, you've made a hilarious mistake.
strategy.advanced: The False-Start Bluff: If you are the dealer or a confident player, make a sudden movement with your hand toward the table without actually slamming. If someone echoes you and slams their hand down prematurely, they are often penalized in house rules.
tips: Pass cards as fast as possible to overwhelm the player to your left. If they are slow, they will have a huge pile of cards to look through, making them less likely to notice someone else winning.
In the 'Stealth' version (Nose-touch), keep a finger near your face at all times.
